The IRS announced that over 1.3 million individuals have approximately $1.2 billion in unclaimed refunds, with a median r ...Individuals who did not file a Form 1040 for the tax year at issue may forfeit refunds if returns are not submitted by April 15. The IRS announced that over 1.3 million individuals have approximately $1.2 billion in unclaimed refunds, with a median refund of $686.Under the law, individuals generally have three years to file returns and claim refunds, after which unclaimed amounts become property of the U.S. Treasury. Individuals who fail to file may also lose eligibility for credits, including the Earned Income Tax Credit, which may significantly increase refund amounts for qualifying individuals.Additionally, refunds may be reduced or offset against outstanding federal or state liabilities, including unpaid taxes, child support, or student loans. The IRS may also hold refunds if returns for subsequent tax years remain unfiled, emphasizing the importance of timely compliance.IR 2026-37© 2026 CCH Incorporated and its affiliates and licensors.
